stem: A bucket's Lifecycle rule is supposed to move 100 KB objects to Standard-IA after 30 days, but a monthly report shows most of those objects never transitioned.

choices.text: The objects are smaller than the 128 KB default minimum size for transition
The rule was scheduled to run before the source class's minimum storage duration elapsed
The bucket has S3 Versioning disabled
The rule targets objects using a prefix filter instead of a tag filter

rationale: By default, only objects of at least 128 KB transition under an S3 Lifecycle rule, so 100 KB objects sit below that floor and never move unless the rule adds an object-size filter to include them. S3 Standard has no minimum storage duration of its own to violate on the way into Standard-IA, so an early-transition timing problem is not what is blocking these objects. Whether S3 Versioning is enabled or disabled does not affect whether a Lifecycle rule's size threshold applies. A Lifecycle rule can filter by prefix or by tag; either filter type still respects the same 128 KB default floor, so the filter type is not the cause.
